text: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David. A song.
Praise awaits you in silence, O God, in Zion; to you the vow shall be fulfilled.
You who hear prayer, to you all flesh shall come.
Deeds of iniquity overwhelm me; our transgressions—you yourself atone for them.

versions.text: When our sins overwhelm me, you atone for our transgressions.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has no possessive on עֲוֺנֹת ("iniquities"); the pronoun shift only comes with פְּשָׁעֵינוּ ("our transgressions"). Saying "our sins overwhelm me" creates an awkward and unwarranted clash of persons within one clause.

versions.text: When iniquities overwhelm me, you atone for our transgressions.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew sets two independent clauses side by side rather than a temporal subordinate clause; rendering the first as "When..." adds a connective the source lacks. It also leaves דִּבְרֵי ("deeds/matters of") unrepresented, and it flattens the emphatic pronoun אַתָּה ("you yourself"), which carries the contrast between human guilt and divine atonement. The revised line keeps the parallel structure and reads well aloud.

text: Blessed is the one you choose and bring near to dwell in your courts. We will be filled with the goodness of your house, the holiness of your temple.
With awesome deeds of righteousness you answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.
You set the mountains in place by your strength, girded with might.

versions.text: You set the mountains in place by your strength, armed with power.
versions.explanation: נֶאְזָר בִּגְבוּרָה is literally "girded with might"; "armed with power" loses the clothing/belt imagery that echoes the "robed/clothed" language later in the psalm (vv. 13-14) and reads less idiomatically in worship context.

text: You still the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples.
Those who live at the ends of the earth stand in awe of your signs; you make the dawn and the sunset shout for joy.
You care for the land and water it; you enrich it abundantly. The streams of God are filled with water to provide the people with grain, for so you have prepared it.
You drench its furrows and level its ridges; you soften it with showers and bless its growth.
You crown the year with your bounty, and your paths overflow with abundance.
The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are robed with joy.
The meadows are clothed with flocks and the valleys are mantled with grain; they shout for joy, they break into song.
